purpose: Directly test canopy-scale hydrodynamic buffering with paired shallow-water velocity measurements and a future quantitative Thalassia endpoint.

motivation.reason_for_direct_measurement: TBOFS grid proximity was generally good but model bathymetry was systematically deeper than the shallow transect record, so model near-bottom sigma velocity is not accepted as literal meadow-scale near-bed exposure.

eligibility.deployment_frame: Census-oriented sampling of baseline-vegetated stable nodes in the three core bays, subject to paired-sensor geometry and field access.
eligibility.secondary_functional_insurance_cohort: All baseline-vegetated nodes, including alternative-seagrass-only nodes.

recent_2023_2025_feasibility_context.boundary: Historical opened data are used only for sampling feasibility; contemporaneous deployment eligibility must be re-evaluated before sensor placement.

eligibility.selection_rule: Apply the frozen contemporaneous baseline rules before deployment. Do not add alternative-only nodes to the primary Thalassia-persistence cohort to rescue sample size, and do not use future outcome for selection or exclusion.

vegetated_sensor_placement.rule: Select the deployment meter mark without using mapped meadow-edge distance.
vegetated_sensor_placement.primary_thalassia_cohort: Among contemporaneous Thalassia-positive meter marks, choose the mark closest to the median site_m of all contemporaneously vegetated meter marks within the node; tie -> lower site_m.
vegetated_sensor_placement.secondary_all_vegetated_cohort: Choose the vegetated mark closest to the median site_m of all contemporaneously vegetated meter marks within the node; tie -> lower site_m.
vegetated_sensor_placement.prohibited_rescue: Do not move the vegetated sensor toward the meadow edge after inspecting bare-control feasibility.

inside_canopy_velocity.requirement: Exact height and instrument geometry frozen before first outcome-bearing deployment.

ambient_reference_velocity.definition: simultaneous velocity above the local canopy at the same node
ambient_reference_velocity.requirement: Reference sampling volume must remain submerged for retained observations; nodes that cannot accommodate frozen paired geometry are primary-ineligible.

deployment.time_alignment: inside and reference records must be simultaneous or reproducibly synchronized

wave_current_resolution_gate.requirement: Retain synchronized burst-level vector velocity at a physically adequate sampling rate to distinguish vector-mean current from oscillatory velocity before any future biological response is opened.
wave_current_resolution_gate.freeze_rule: Sampling rate, burst duration, and burst interval may be chosen from instrument specifications plus a response-independent physical pilot only; they cannot be tuned against Thalassia outcomes.
wave_current_resolution_gate.failure_boundary: If the instrument stores only long-interval vector averages that erase oscillatory velocity, the study is a current-only exposure study and must not claim broad wave-plus-current hydrodynamic buffering.

baseline_canopy_context: local shoot density under a frozen quadrat protocol
canopy cover or frozen photographic equivalent
species-specific local cover/occupancy of Thalassia, Halodule, Syringodium and other structural macrophytes

canopy_counterfactual_control.purpose: Separate vegetation-associated flow attenuation from the ordinary seabed boundary-layer vertical velocity gradient.
canopy_counterfactual_control.cohort: Nested response-independent physical-validation subset; nodes may remain in the primary future-persistence cohort even when no valid bare control exists.

control_geometry.habitat: nearby unvegetated or effectively canopy-free seabed
control_geometry.requirement: No obvious channel edge, shoreline barrier, inlet jet, structure, or other feature that would make ambient forcing non-comparable. Record substrate and bathymetric context before looking at any future biological response.
control_geometry.reference_origin: The <=100 m separation is measured from the preselected vegetated deployment meter mark, not from transect start and not from an edge-nearest mark chosen after GIS inspection.

canopy_counterfactual_control.sensors: Use the same frozen near-bed and above-canopy/above-bed sampling heights and the same instrument family/QC on vegetated and bare patches. Prefer fully simultaneous four-volume measurement; if hardware limits force staggered deployment, the node is not eligible for the confirmatory canopy-attribution gate.
canopy_counterfactual_control.physical_attribution_gate: Using a node-level paired bootstrap fixed before inspection, the 95% interval for mean excess_canopy_attenuation_p90 must lie above 0. If not, do not attribute the vertical attenuation metric specifically to canopy ecosystem engineering.

spatial_preflight.interpretation: The 18-node nested counterfactual target is geographically feasible. GIS proximity is only reconnaissance; every retained control must still pass the frozen field depth/forcing/substrate/wake/simultaneity rules.

representative_placement_preflight.interpretation: The counterfactual remains geographically feasible when the vegetated sensor position is selected independently of edge proximity.

primary_physical_metrics.ambient_p90: 90th percentile of valid synchronized reference-layer horizontal current speed after the frozen short-window aggregation
primary_physical_metrics.physical_gate: Report node-level attenuation_p90 distribution and frozen node-level uncertainty before linking to future biological outcome.
primary_physical_metrics.burst_statistic_rule: Use the same pre-frozen burst/short-window velocity statistic at inside-canopy and reference sensors. The statistic must be defined before future biological response access.

future_outcome.primary: next fixed-transect survey focal_frequency minus baseline focal_frequency
secondary: next survey Braun-Blanquet all-point index minus baseline
next survey blade length minus baseline where observed
next survey shoot density minus baseline where observed

primary_analysis.directional_hypothesis: higher attenuation_p90 predicts more positive / less negative future focal-frequency change
primary_analysis.uncertainty: node-level bootstrap or permutation rule frozen before outcome access
primary_analysis.missing_data_rule: complete-case primary analysis after only predeclared instrument/QC exclusions

secondary_mechanism_support.canopy_structure: canopy height, local shoot density and cover may be related descriptively or under one predeclared corrected secondary family to attenuation_p90
secondary_mechanism_support.turbidity_pathway: optional co-located turbidity / suspended-sediment measurement may test whether attenuation reduces near-bed resuspension
secondary_mechanism_support.boundary: Secondary variables cannot replace a null primary attenuation result.

community_functional_insurance.question: Does local species composition explain measured attenuation_p90 after total vegetated cover and canopy height are represented?
community_functional_insurance.motivation: Existing Tampa exact-point analyses show pooled persistence of pre-existing alternative seagrasses after focal loss, but the stable-node audit does not resolve a local insurance effect and functional equivalence is unknown. Multispecies canopy structure can alter near-bed flow.
community_functional_insurance.inference: two-sided secondary coefficient for thalassia_fraction under the declared secondary multiple-testing family
community_functional_insurance.interpretation: A composition effect would show that retained seagrass occupancy is not automatically hydrodynamically equivalent; a null effect would be consistent with functional redundancy only within the sampled range and uncertainty.
community_functional_insurance.boundary: Secondary test cannot rescue a null primary attenuation-to-future-frequency result.
community_functional_insurance.cohort: All baseline-vegetated core nodes, including alternative-only nodes; analyze physical attenuation, not future Thalassia persistence, as the endpoint.

metrics: oscillatory horizontal RMS speed after removal of the burst vector mean
wave_current_decomposition.role: Physical interpretation of why attenuation varies among canopies.
wave_current_decomposition.boundary: Secondary current-versus-oscillatory decomposition cannot replace or rescue a null primary attenuation_p90 result.

relationship_to_clonal_contract.rule: Do not build a combined TNC x hydrodynamic model after future outcome inspection. Any integration must be separately frozen in advance.

pre_outcome_freeze_required: response-independent physical pilot rule for sampling rate / burst duration / burst interval
bare-control maximum separation and depth-matching rule
paired-bootstrap rule for the canopy-attribution gate
representative vegetated meter-mark selection rule independent of mapped edge distance
claim_boundary: The design tests measured canopy-scale physical buffering prospectively; it does not infer hydrodynamics from annual biological state.
Shoot density alone is not accepted as a proxy for hydrodynamic attenuation.
A supported attenuation coefficient is consistent with self-facilitation but does not by itself prove causal ecosystem engineering.
Do not change velocity percentile, sensor height, subgroup or endpoint after future response access to rescue a null primary result.
Do not call binary re-recording recovery.
Do not label the future attenuation association as a decisive null if fewer than 30 analyzable nodes remain; below the frozen precision gate it is a pilot estimate.
Alternative-seagrass-only nodes may strengthen the secondary functional-insurance physical test but must not be counted toward the primary future Thalassia-persistence sample-size gate.
If stored velocity cannot resolve oscillatory motion, restrict claims to current-speed attenuation; do not generalize to wave buffering.
Inside-versus-above-canopy velocity contrast alone is not sufficient to attribute attenuation to vegetation because ordinary seabed boundary-layer shear can create the same vertical pattern.
Use the term canopy ecosystem engineering / hydrodynamic self-facilitation only if the nested bare-bed counterfactual physical gate and the prospective future-state gate both pass.
Do not choose an edge-nearest vegetated deployment mark after inspection to manufacture a nearby bare control.

design_precision_gate.planning_model_terms: baseline_frequency + ambient_p90 + attenuation_p90 + two water-body indicators
design_precision_gate.planning_assumption: Approximate Gaussian multiple-regression benchmark, two-sided alpha 0.05, 80% power for the attenuation term; used only to prevent an underpowered confirmatory label.
design_precision_gate.primary_rule: The future attenuation-to-Thalassia-frequency analysis is confirmatory only with at least 30 baseline-Thalassia-positive analyzable nodes and at least 8 such nodes in each core bay. Below that gate, report effect estimates and uncertainty as a pilot and do not use a null result to reject hydrodynamic buffering.
design_precision_gate.interpretation: The recent historical frame suggests roughly 33 primary-eligible nodes, so the primary test is principally powered for moderate-to-large partial effects. Alternative-only nodes improve the secondary functional-insurance physical contrast but do not increase primary persistence sample size.

ecosystem_engineering_feedback_gate.purpose: Require both the physical engineering link and the prospective ecological persistence link before using a self-facilitation interpretation.
ecosystem_engineering_feedback_gate.gate_A_physical: The nested bare-bed counterfactual physical-attribution gate passes.
ecosystem_engineering_feedback_gate.gate_B_future_ecology: The prespecified primary attenuation_p90 coefficient predicts more positive / less negative future focal-frequency change under the existing prospective model and frozen alpha/uncertainty rule.

interpretation.both_pass: Results are consistent with hydrodynamic self-facilitation: vegetation-associated attenuation is physically demonstrated and stronger attenuation predicts greater subsequent Thalassia quantitative stability.
interpretation.A_pass_B_fail: Canopy-associated flow engineering is demonstrated, but no supported link to future Thalassia stability is established.
interpretation.A_fail_B_pass: Attenuation predicts future state, but canopy causation is not identified; describe a hydrodynamic-state association, not ecosystem engineering.

ecosystem_engineering_feedback_gate.boundary: This two-gate rule is still observational at the meadow scale and does not prove a causal positive feedback without experimental manipulation.
